tagline.text: A seafood market and cook-to-order dining strip on Macapagal Boulevard in Pasay, where your pick of the catch is cooked on the spot

location.label: Location
location.text: Diosdado Macapagal Boulevard (Macapagal Blvd), Pasay City, near SM Mall of Asia

children.text: A Filipino-style seafood market and dining strip on Macapagal Boulevard in Pasay. Pick shrimp, crab and shellfish straight from the tanks, hand them to a nearby restaurant, and have them cooked just the way you like. Once you know how haggling and cooking charges work, you can enjoy fresh seafood in a lively local atmosphere.

Dampa is a Tagalog word for a temporary hut or simple eatery, and today it refers to the practice of buying seafood at a market and having a restaurant cook it for you. Dampa Seafood Market is a leading dampa on Diosdado Macapagal Boulevard in Pasay City, and the city government's tourism page describes it as one of the largest and most popular seafood destinations in Metro Manila. It is commonly called "Seaside Dampa," "New Dampa Seaside" or "Dampa sa Pasay," and all of these names refer to the market and restaurant area here.

The setup is simple. On one side of the street, stalls sell shrimp, crab, lobster, squid, shellfish and fish from tanks and beds of ice, while on the opposite side and behind them, "paluto" restaurants, which cook the ingredients you bring, stand in a row. You agree on a price at the stall after the seafood is weighed, a restaurant staff member then escorts you and your purchase to the kitchen, and you choose a cooking style such as grilled, fried, steamed or garlic butter. The biggest quirk is that the market price and the restaurant's cooking charge are billed separately.

The mood is closer to a bustling market than to an upscale seafood restaurant. Many vendors call out to passersby, and it gets crowded on weekend evenings. In return, you get generous platters and the cheerful feel of local family and birthday gatherings, and the need to haggle makes it a good way to experience Philippine market culture. Hours and the mix of businesses can change, so please check the latest information before you go.

If it is your first visit, start by walking the whole stretch of stalls to get a feel for the place. Many reviews mention aggressive touting, so it is best to compare prices at several stalls before deciding. Korean travelers usually build their order around shrimp and crab and add a shellfish or fish dish or two. Prices vary with the season and the size of the seafood, so the amounts in this guide are only a reference, and asking on the spot is the most accurate way to find out.

blocks.title: Seafood you pick from the tanks

children.text: Shrimp, crab, lobster, shellfish, squid, scallops and many kinds of fish are displayed at each stall. You can judge the condition with your own eyes, which gives great confidence in freshness. It is best to walk around the stalls once, comparing prices and sizes, before you buy.

Bring your chosen ingredients to a restaurant and they will cook them grilled, fried, steamed, in garlic butter, in chili sauce, in salted egg sauce and more. The prices on the menu are cooking charges, not the price of the ingredients. You can also ask for one ingredient to be split and cooked in two or three different ways.

Garlic butter prawns, fried crab in chili sauce, baked scallops with cheese, oyster omelets, chili-lime crab and fried squid rings are frequently mentioned. Filipino-style shellfish dishes and fresh grilled fish also go well with rice.

It is normal to bargain down from the first price a stall quotes. The more you buy at once, the easier the negotiation, so going with a group is an advantage. Get into the habit of watching the scale with the vendor when the seafood is weighed.

The dining area has a range of businesses, including Chinese-style and Filipino grill-style restaurants, and some have karaoke facilities used for group gatherings. Atmosphere and cooking charges differ by restaurant, so it is best to look at the cooking-charge menu first before you decide.

Because it lies on Macapagal Boulevard in the Manila Bay reclamation area, SM Mall of Asia, the Entertainment City hotels and casinos, and the Aseana City malls are all nearby. It is a convenient spot for dinner between shopping or other plans.

Some reviewers say you can try local ingredients such as kohol (apple snail) and lato (sea grapes) in addition to ordinary shrimp and crab. Adding one or two things you have never eaten before makes the dampa experience richer.

blocks.title: A scale that suits families and groups

children.text: One serving is generous and works well for 4–6 people to share, while reviews note that it can feel relatively expensive for one or two diners. The more people you have, the more varieties you can buy in small amounts and taste in different styles.

items.title: Dinner course
items.subtitle: A walk through the market, then paluto

children.text: Arrive at Macapagal Boulevard. If you go early, before sunset, it is less crowded and easier to find parking and a table.
Walk the stalls and compare prices. Decide what you want to buy (shrimp, crab, shellfish, fish) and roughly how much.
Haggle at a stall you like, check the weight and buy. Paying in cash is easiest.
Go to the kitchen area with a restaurant staff member, order how you want it cooked, and order rice and drinks.
Finish your meal and check the cooking charges, service charge and taxes on the bill.
The time needed depends on the size of your group and cooking time. The more people you have, the more dishes you can order to share, which makes it more efficient.
Shop at SM Mall of Asia or walk along the Manila Bay promenade.
Watch the Manila Bay sunset, then go by car to Macapagal Boulevard.
Choose seafood at the Dampa market and order your dishes at a restaurant.
To avoid traffic jams around Manila Bay and MOA, use Grab or a taxi and allow plenty of time for the trip back.
You can reach it by Grab or taxi from anywhere in Manila, such as Makati, BGC or Malate. Enter "Dampa sa Pasay" or "Dampa Seaside Macapagal, Diosdado Macapagal Blvd" as the destination.
From SM Mall of Asia it is a short drive. Directions describe going from Seaside Boulevard onto Macapagal Boulevard.

The LRT-1 Redemptorist–Aseana station opened in November 2024, but the market is a long way to walk from it, so taking a taxi or Grab from the station is the safer choice. Check current routes and fares locally.
It is a short ride by taxi or Grab from Ninoy Aquino International Airport. At rush hour, when traffic is heavy, the trip can take much longer.
Going straight from the airport for dinner and then on to your hotel is awkward if you have luggage, so it is better to drop your bags at your hotel first.
If you drive, there is parking nearby, but reviews say spaces run short at busy times. It is best to go early.
On the way back, Macapagal Boulevard gets congested at rush hour and on weekend evenings, so allow plenty of time for your Grab pickup.

The types and prices of seafood vary with the season, weather and catch. On days when typhoons or rough seas make conditions poor, prices can rise or the selection can shrink. To avoid crowds, an early weekday evening is the most comfortable time, and queues can be long on weekend evenings.

Since the dampa itself is the place to eat, staying near Macapagal Boulevard makes getting around easy, such as in the Pasay and Parañaque Bay area, around MOA, or at hotels in Aseana City and Entertainment City. It is also close to the airport, so it works well for dinner on your first or last night.

Remember that the cooking charge and the price of the ingredients are separate. If you split one ingredient into two or three cooking styles, the number of dishes goes up and so can the cooking charge. Portions often feed 4–6 people, so decide the weight of the ingredients according to your group size, and buying a little at first and then more if it is not enough is also a good approach.

Cooking style names and prices differ from restaurant to restaurant, so photographing the menu before you order makes it easier to check against the bill. Rice and drinks are ordered separately, and you can ask for the spiciness of the sauce or the amount of garlic to be adjusted. Cooking can take a while, so order drinks first in the meantime. If someone in your group does not eat seafood, ask in advance whether a nearby restaurant can serve chicken or pork dishes separately.
Bring plenty of cash. Reviews say many businesses do not accept cards.
Go early. Arriving before sunset helps you avoid crowds and find parking more easily.
Look around several stalls before buying. Even for the same shrimp, size and price differ from stall to stall.
Check the scale together before buying and agree exactly on the price. It is best not to settle weight and unit price by word of mouth alone.
Check the cooking-charge menu and the service charge before choosing a restaurant. A service charge and taxes are added to the bill.
Do not simply follow touts. You may be steered to a particular restaurant, so take your time deciding.
If you have a seafood allergy, tell the staff clearly before the dish is cooked.
Many places let you take leftovers home. If there is a lot of food, ask for a doggy bag.
Cooking time can run long depending on group size and how busy it is, so allow plenty of time.
If you do not confirm prices and how the bill is calculated, the total may be much higher than you expect. Always check the unit price, the weight and the cooking charge before you buy.
It is a crowded place, so keep a close eye on your phone and wallet.
Touts may steer you to a particular stall or restaurant, so refuse clearly and choose for yourself.
Raw or undercooked shellfish and oysters can cause hygiene problems, so eat them fully cooked and avoid them if you are not feeling well.
Hours and the mix of businesses can change, so check the latest announcements before you go.
During the rainy season and at rush hour, Macapagal Boulevard is congested, so leave room in your plans for the trip home.
A large shopping mall a short drive away. It is a good place to add shopping or a stroll before or after eating at the dampa.
A shoreline with a promenade and sunsets over Manila Bay. A common plan is to follow the sunset with dinner at the dampa.
A well-known church near the LRT-1 Baclaran station, visited by many worshippers for the Wednesday novena.
A cultural center complex near Roxas Boulevard, where you can build a plan of seeing a show or exhibition and eating seafood in the evening.
